clue.text: Half of Western state for Muslim leader

indicators.note: half of means only the opening five of the state's ten letters are kept

parts.note: California is a state in the western USA

explanation.surface: A clue about splitting an American state in two to install a religious ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: CALIF is also the standard short form of California, so the first half of the state's name is a familiar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph, also spelt calif, was the civil and religious head of the Muslim world.

definitions.meaning: something sure to happen, a sure thing
a horse thought bound to win is called a racing dead cert

explanation.surface: A tip about a racehorse that is bound to win.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a sure thing, and racing slang for a horse considered certain to win.

indicators.note: upset means the name's letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: c, short for the Latin circa, means about

explanation.surface: Raquel is cross about her hair spray.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a hairspray that holds a style in place, a kind of hair-dressing.

indicators.note: say tells us the word for gala is spoken, and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a fete is a gala or outdoor festival

explanation.surface: Fortune-telling at a village festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate is one's destiny or lot, a synonym of fortune.

clue.text: Excellent golf-score shot by the Coleridge character

definitions.meaning: three strokes under par on a hole, rarer than an eagle
the seabird killed with a crossbow by the Ancient Mariner in Coleridge's poem

explanation.surface: A golfer's dream score set beside a famous literary killing.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf it names a score of three under par; in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner it is the seabird the mariner shoots.

clue.text: Bourgeois hand-shake that provides a pension?

indicators.note: shake tells us the letters of the two words before it are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A middle-class handshake that secures a retirement pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pension' looks like retirement money, but in French a pension is a guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension, in French and in Europe, is a small hotel or guesthouse providing lodging and meals.

definitions.meaning: a drop that runs down the cheek when crying
a rip or split in fabric

explanation.surface: A small cut in the rent payment, cheekily made.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a drop of crying on a cheek, and also a rip, which is what rent means as a noun.

definitions.meaning: a hospital worker who moves patients and does general tasks

explanation.surface: Praise for a polite hospital worker.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means disciplined and calm; as a noun it is a hospital porter or assistant.

indicators.note: returning means the little word is goes back to front

parts.note: new means anew or afresh

explanation.surface: Getting one's strength back all over again.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means a tendon, and by extension muscular power or strength.

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the clue's first word are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concerning a poetry evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but is the anagram signal for ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a public performance, such as reading poems aloud to an audience.

clue.text: 0.0, a quiz result, it turns out, in the French style

indicators.note: it turns out signals that the letters before it are turned into a new order

parts.note: each zero gives the letter O

explanation.surface: A quiz scoring nothing at all, revealed in French fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turns out' sounds like 'as it happens' but is the anagram signal for OO A QUIZ RESULT.
explanation.definitionFit: This names the ornate style of furniture and decoration of the reign of Louis XIV of France.

parts.note: a band is a musical group
on, as in a show or record being on, means playing

explanation.surface: A pop group performing out in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone is to leave them in the lurch, a verb sense of desert.

clue.text: A strange family of lords and ladies !

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An odd aristocratic family, exclamation mark and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lords and ladies' sounds like the peerage but is the country name for the wild cuckoo-pint plant, of the genus Arum.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords-and-ladies (cuckoo-pint) is a wild plant of the Arum genus, so Arum is its botanical group.

clue.text: Conduct is mainly good in Scotland

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened word goes inside the Scots word for good

parts.note: gude is the Scots spelling of good, as the clue's Scotland signals

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word is, keeping just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A comment on Scottish standards of behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct a visitor round a place is to lead or escort them, a verb sense of guide.

indicators.note: back tells us the word for keeping is read from right to left

parts.note: ward means keeping or custody, as in being in someone's ward

explanation.surface: An artist holding back a sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a picture is to sketch it, a straightforward synonym.

indicators.note: in tells us the chemical symbol goes inside the word for tough

parts.note: hard means tough or difficult
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Keeping an oxygen supply in harsh conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' only rounds off the surface: HARD is the surrounding piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a hidden stock or store kept back, a reserve.

clue.text: Right line, they say, in Cornwall

indicators.note: they say tells us the two words are spoken together and their sound gives the answer

parts.note: true means right or correct; a row is a line

explanation.surface: Speaking of a correct railway line in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Truro is the cathedral city of Cornwall, in south-west England; the definition reads as 'a city in Cornwall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is the county town and only city of Cornwall.

clue.text: Edgy drive? On US green, very tricky!

indicators.note: tricky signals that the four words before it are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A golfer feeling jittery about a treacherous American putting green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' and 'green' suggest golf, but 'tricky' is the anagram signal for ON US GREEN VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means the restless, jittery vigour produced by anxiety, an edgy kind of drive.

clue.text: Minister took meals in his office

parts.note: a pastor is a minister of a church
ate means took meals

explanation.surface: A clergyman dining at his desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorate is the post or term of a minister of a church, so his office is a pastorate.

clue.text: Change not required for journeys in them?

definitions.text: Change not required for journeys in them?

parts.words: Change not required for journeys in them?
parts.note: 'change' looks like coins, but means changing from one railway service to another; these services run direct to the destination

explanation.surface: Travel advice about not needing coins for a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: These are rail services that run the whole route, so passengers need not switch at any station.

parts.note: 'purchase' looks like shopping, but means a grip; a climber's tiny grip room for a foot on rock

explanation.surface: A mountaineer buying something small.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small foothold just big enough for the front of a foot, a climber's slight grip.

clue.text: Such lassitude — one in ten with air-conditioning!

indicators.note: in tells us the single letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
conditioning signals that the letters of ten and air are worked into a new form

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Feeling sluggish thanks to air-conditioning, one person in ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness or lack of energy, the state of lassitude.

definitions.meaning: a joint of meat, as in a roast
a grumble or grievance, in slang

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding grumble about an aching joint.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cut of meat for roasting, and slang for a gripe or grievance.

clue.text: Derogatory name for a woman's broom

definitions.meaning: a dialect insult for a slatternly woman
a brush of twigs bound to a handle

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a woman about her broom.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old term of abuse for a woman, and a broom of twigs, as a witch rides.

definitions.meaning: a dark beer, close kin to the strong dark ale brewed as a stronger porter

explanation.surface: A description of a heavily built railway porter.
explanation.definitionFit: It means thickset or portly, and it is also a strong dark beer derived from porter.

indicators.note: inner tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: The usual setting inside a household freezer.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero degrees is a specific temperature, freezing point on the Celsius scale.

clue.text: Sunday gear for this piece of satire?

parts.note: kit means gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one's Sunday best is fit for a comic sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch that mocks something, a piece of satire.

indicators.note: amongst tells us the letters lie among the words that follow

explanation.surface: Basil planted among other bedding plants in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' looks like a man's name, but is the kitchen plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an example of an aromatic plant used in cooking.

parts.note: Potters Bar is a Hertfordshire town, but read here as the place or game where someone pots balls on a table

explanation.surface: A reference to Potters Bar, a commuter town just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cue game in which players pot balls, so the potter's pub game is this one.

clue.text: Complex girl to vote for Con stable, for instance

parts.note: to elect someone is to vote for them
John Constable the painter was an RA, a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A girl voting for a police constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con stable' splits the painter John Constable's name to suggest a police officer; he was a Royal Academician, RA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Electra was the daughter of Agamemnon, and Jung named a daughter's father fixation the Electra complex after her.

clue.text: Changing horses in it, I'd stammer nervously

indicators.note: nervously signals that the words before it are scrambled into another order

explanation.surface: A speaker stammering anxiously about switching horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says don't change horses in midstream, meaning don't switch plans halfway through.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns against swapping horses halfway across a river, a time and place this phrase names.

parts.note: an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: A British title-holding duo.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is two of something, especially game birds, so it means a couple.
